text:
emily: quick follow-up from the v2 weights RFC — i wanted to float a narrower design for shard placement hints and ABI compatibility
kai: nice, high-level?
emily: goal: let model-builders express colocation preferences without forcing on-disk format changes that break mmap paths
srini: we hit this in perf tests — cross-node shard fetches spike tail latency. placement hints would help routing + prefetch decisions.
alex: are we talking metadata in the manifest, or an opaque header in each safetensors shard?
emily: manifest-level hints + optional per-shard tag. manifest stays backward compatible: if old runtime sees unknown hint -> ignore. new runtime reads hint for allocation.
tara: how does this interact with private deployments where nodes have different disk topologies? e.g., NVMe vs network storage?
kai: placement_hint should be advisory: values like "prefer-same-host", "spread-across-racks", or "require-local". runtime translates to placement policies per cluster.
srini: small nit: "require-local" can't be honored if shards are too large to fit. need a pin_priority + fallback order.
emily: exactly. proposal: WeightLocator v2 adds fields: placement_hint (string), pin_priority (int), preferred_nodes (optional list). Old locator stays valid; loader ignores unknown fields.
alex: preferred_nodes is tricky — leaks infra into model artifact. maybe keep it as hint: node labels or affinity tags rather than concrete hostnames.
emily: agreed, use labels. we should document that preferred_nodes may be ignored.
srini: runtime work: packing algorithm picks shards with same placement_hint into the same allocation group. fallback: greedy pack by free GB then by rack tag.
tara: what about mmap path? we still want to support memory-mapped safetensors with sparse-index on disk. If we add per-shard headers, mmap offset calculation must remain stable.
kai: solution: keep on-disk payload identical + add a small sidecar index file (safetensors.meta.json) for v2 hints. Loader tries sidecar first, falls back to in-shard legacy parsing. No mmap ABI break.
alex: sidecar file sounds safe. any atomicity concerns on upload? we need an artifact upload step that writes shard + sidecar atomically or an upload manifest with checksum.
emily: propose upload flow: 1) upload shards (immutable) 2) upload manifest v2 with checksums + sidecar entries 3) server verifies checksums and publishes model version. If manifest v2 is present, runtime will consult it for placement hints.
srini: that also helps rollbacks: manifest points to exact shard checksums. runtime can detect mismatch and refuse to load incompatible sets.
tara: warmup implications: if placement_hint="prefer-same-host", warmup scheduler will try to prioritize bringing those shards into local NVMe first. If not available, it triggers a prefetch from remote.
kai: and pin_priority controls eviction: high priority => less likely to evict cache entries during pressure. Good for small-model critical shards.
alex: do we need encryption metadata in sidecar? Private deployments will want KMS references.
emily: sidecar schema includes kms_key_id (optional) and checksum. If kms_key_id present, runtime uses customer KMS to decrypt. Again optional to preserve simplicity for public hosted mode.
srini: test checklist?
emily: short list:
- loader ignores unknown manifest fields (backcompat)
- sidecar used when present, fallback works if missing
- placement_hint semantics tested on single-host and multi-rack clusters
- mmap users see no ABI changes and checksum mismatch errors are clear
- warmup respects pin_priority and placement_hint
tara: one more: monitoring impact — add metric placement_hint_applied{model, hint} and warmup_prefetch_remote{model}=count to see when hints are being ignored or cause remote fetches.
deploy-bot: reminder: RFC follow-up meeting scheduled Thu 10:00 for final sign-off :calendar:
emily: thanks. i'll draft the manifest v2 schema + upload flow PR and link it in the thread. please poke at the edge cases above before Thu. :thumbsup:
